brief.topic: Improving HTML-to-Markdown Extraction with Local LLMs
brief.problem_or_goal: Discussing methods and challenges for enhancing HTML-to-Markdown conversion using local LLMs, aiming to outperform traditional tools on complex websites.
brief.context: A community member is sharing their experience and seeking advice on a project that uses local LLMs (Qwen2.5-7B/8B with llama.cpp) to convert HTML web pages to Markdown, focusing on offline processing and improved quality over standard tools. The project aims to handle difficult website structures like SPAs and noisy sites.
brief.motivation: The original author is seeking feedback and solutions for specific challenges encountered in their HTML-to-Markdown conversion project, particularly concerning media-heavy sites, performance optimization, and evaluation methods. This discussion aims to gather insights from other local LLM users.
brief.desired_response: Community members are invited to share their approaches, tips, and recommendations for improving the HTML-to-Markdown extraction process, especially for challenging web content, and to discuss the potential usefulness of such a tool.
brief.speaker_relationship_to_source: reader of archived source; no claim of personally running reported tests

facts.text: The project aims to convert HTML web pages to high-quality Markdown using local LLMs (Qwen2.5-7B/8B, llama.cpp) running on consumer GPUs, fully offline.
facts.evidence_quote: I'm working on a smarter way to convert HTML web pages to high-quality Markdown using **local LLMs** (Qwen2.5-7B/8B, llama.cpp) running on consumer GPUs. My goal: outperform traditional tools like Readability or html2text on tricky websites (e.g. modern SPAs, tech blogs, and noisy sites) — and do it all *fully offline*, without sending data to cloud APIs.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The script analyzes if a site is text-focused or media-centric and uses BeautifulSoup to extract candidate content areas, main titles, headings, and framework fingerprints.
facts.evidence_quote:
My script first analyzes if a site is text-focused or media-centric (e.g. video/image/social), with structural and domain heuristics.
* **HTML structure analysis:** Uses BeautifulSoup to extract candidate content areas, main titles, headings, and framework fingerprints (React, Vue, WordPress, etc).
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: A local LLM generates JSON-formatted extraction strategies and scores the content for completeness, readability, and info value after Markdown extraction.
facts.evidence_quote:
Local LLM generates JSON-formatted extraction strategies (selectors, noise filters, special rules) for each page, not just using static rules.
* **AI quality scoring:** After Markdown extraction, the LLM scores content for completeness, readability, info value, and offers improvement advice.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The tool runs locally using llama-cpp-python with quantized GGUF models on hardware like a 4070/4080/4090 or a 7B model on a MacBook.
facts.evidence_quote: I use llama-cpp-python with quantized GGUF models, so it runs on a 4070/4080/4090 or even a 7B model on a MacBook.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: On standard article/news/blog pages, the AI assessment scores quality as typically 'good' or 'excellent' (7-9/10).
facts.evidence_quote: On standard article/news/blog pages, quality is usually “good” or “excellent” (AI assessment scores 7-9/10).
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: For media-heavy or JavaScript-only sites, the LLM struggles without browser rendering.
facts.evidence_quote: For *media-heavy* or JavaScript-only sites, even the LLM struggles without browser rendering.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The overall speed is decent (one page ≈ 10–20 sec on 4070 8G, q4_K_M), but batch processing hundreds of pages could be faster.
facts.evidence_quote: The overall speed is decent (one page ≈ 10–20 sec on 4070 8G, q4\_K\_M), but batch processing hundreds of pages could be faster.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement
